script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 14. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Children ask around 300 questions a day.  Adults?  About 20.

When you're genuinely curious, your brain floods with dopamine—the same chemical involved in anticipation and reward. This doesn't just feel good; it physically enhances your hippocampus's ability to form memories. Curiosity is nature's learning drug. Here's what's amazing: the memory boost from curiosity spills over.  If you're curious about one topic, you'll remember unrelated information presented at the same time better too.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You don't lose curiosity—you suppress it.  That wondering child is still inside you, buried under the need to seem like you already know.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Curiosity Revival - Ask More Questions.

Here's your activity: Today, ask at least three genuine questions—at work, at home, or to yourself. Not rhetorical questions. Real ones you want answered. Notice how asking changes how you engage with the world. This helps you reclaim your natural curiosity through deliberate questioning.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why curious people learn more can be applied to curiosity revival - ask more questions. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
